passage: In the college library, Mehak stood at the window with her phone on video, while Mahima sat in a hostel room across the city. "Give me your dates." "Internals start on the ninth, finals on the twenty-second." Mehak typed both into a shared calendar in blue. "Mine are red. The fifth to the eighteenth." They looked at the screen: a solid block of colour. "So fewer calls those weeks. Two short ones?" "Two short ones, and no guilt." Mehak added a green star after the twenty-second: "Long call, no books." Mahima smiled at it. A student at the next table looked up, and Mehak lowered her voice, still smiling. That night neither wondered what a quiet day meant.

qa.q: What colour did Mehak use for Mahima's exam dates?
qa.a: Mehak used blue for Mahima's exam dates.

qa.q: What is Mahima feeling when she sees the green star?
qa.a: Mahima feels happy and reassured, smiling at the planned long call after the exams.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the couple add if one of them still worries during exam weeks, and why?
qa.a: They could agree on one short check-in message, because a small agreed signal covers the gap when full calls are paused.

qa.q: How might the student at the next table see Mehak on the phone?
qa.a: The student looks up at the voice in the library, so the student sees a person quietly having a personal call and not a distraction from work.

grounding: Shows a couple marking exam weeks on a shared calendar, agreeing on fewer calls then, and planning a longer catch-up afterward.

passage:
Hi Vivek,
Since we keep missing each other in exam season, I tried something. Anjali, my roommate, showed me how she and her boyfriend use a shared calendar, so I made one for us. It's in your inbox.
I've marked my exam weeks in red: 2 to 13 December. Can you mark yours in blue? I think yours are in the second half of November.
My suggestion for those weeks: two short calls, Wednesday and Sunday, fifteen minutes each, just to hear each other. No long talks, no big topics. Then, the day after the last exam for whichever of us finishes later, a proper evening call, as long as we want. I've already put 14 December in green for that.
I don't want to feel guilty for studying, and I don't want you to feel ignored.
Mark your weeks when you can.
Sarita

qa.q: Which dates did Sarita mark in red?
What does the line 'I don't want to feel guilty for studying' show about Sarita?
qa.a: It shows Sarita feels torn between exams and the relationship, and worried that Vivek might feel ignored.

qa.q: What could Sarita and Vivek do if an exam date moves?
qa.a: Update the shared calendar at once and shift the green catch-up day, so the plan stays accurate.

qa.q: How might Vivek feel opening the shared calendar?
qa.a: Vivek may feel reassured, since fewer calls in December come with a reason and a long call already booked for after.

grounding: Shows a couple marking each other's exam weeks on a shared calendar, agreeing to fewer, shorter calls then, and planning a long catch-up after.

passage:
Hrithik, you asked how Nishat and I didn't break up during finals. So here it is, from Asif, the man who used to call her every night even when she had a paper at nine.
Last semester was a disaster. She was studying, I kept calling, she'd pick up out of guilt, and we'd both be short with each other. Then she'd have a bad paper, and so would I.
This time we did it differently. In October we opened one shared calendar and each shaded our exam weeks. Hers began on the 18th of November, mine on the 25th. For those weeks we agreed: one good-luck message before each exam, and a ten-minute call on Sundays only. Nothing else, no guilt.
And we booked the evening of 12 December, the day after my last paper, for a long video call with dinner ordered on both sides.
Easiest exam season we've had. That dinner call went on for three hours.

qa.q: What did Asif and Nishat agree for exam weeks?
qa.a: One good-luck message before each exam, and a ten-minute call on Sundays only.

qa.q: How does Asif feel now about last semester's nightly calls?
qa.a: He feels regretful, seeing that calling every night made them both short-tempered and hurt their papers.

qa.q: What else could Asif and Nishat add for the next exam season?
qa.a: A simple way to say if one of them is struggling badly, so the reduced contact never leaves someone alone at a hard moment.

qa.q: How might the new plan have felt for Nishat?
qa.a: Nishat could study without picking up out of guilt, and still knew a long call was waiting on 12 December.

grounding: Shows a couple shading exam weeks on a shared calendar, cutting to short contact then, and booking a long catch-up after.
